claims.text: Adding titanium to a Cantor-based high-entropy alloy will improve its wear resistance under tribo-corrosion conditions.
Adding titanium to a Cantor-based high-entropy alloy will improve its corrosion protection under tribo-corrosion conditions.
Titanium addition will refine the microstructure of the Cantor-based alloy.
Titanium addition will enhance passive-film stability in the Cantor-based alloy.
Microstructural refinement can improve the wear resistance of high-entropy alloys.
A more stable passive film can improve corrosion resistance.
Microstructure governs corrosion behavior in Cantor alloys.
Refining the Cantor-alloy microstructure will improve its corrosion protection.
The coupled tribo-corrosion response is governed by the combined effects of microstructural refinement and passive-film stabilization.
The titanium-modified alloy will outperform an otherwise matched titanium-free Cantor-based alloy in both wear and corrosion protection.
The improvement will be greatest at moderate titanium contents of approximately 1–2%.
Benefits may decrease at titanium contents above or below the proposed moderate range.
Comparing titanium contents of 0, 0.5, 1, and 1.5% under controlled tribo-corrosion conditions provides a titanium-free control and a composition series.
Wear resistance, corrosion protection, microstructure, and passive-film stability will be measured in the controlled comparison.
Failure of titanium addition to improve wear resistance and corrosion protection would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the proposed microstructural refinement or passive-film stabilization would falsify the proposed mechanism.
The exact way titanium affects microstructure and passive-film stability is not fully understood.
